Decided ghost 11 of 27: #werk-chat-turn-id.

What it says: Every message the person sends gets a turn name when the browser sends it.

The agent runs one turn at a time. The server keeps the sent turns in order, until each one ends.
Each part of the agent's reply belongs to the oldest open turn. The end line closes that turn, and the next one starts.
The live channel carries the turn name with each part.
Two edge cases: if the agent exits, each open turn gets the exit as its end. A part for a turn that this page did not send, such as after a reload, starts a new turn.
What it shows: Message A "Summarise the open cards" and message B "Also list the ghosts", sent while the reply to A streams. A five-step example and a chart show the parts of reply A landing above B, and the first part of reply B landing under B.

What is good:

The reason is a real bug. The pane adds every part at the bottom, so the rest of reply A reads as the answer to B.
depends_on werk-progress is decided, and the end line comes from it. Both rejected options are recorded: "draw a message only when its turn starts" and "a new message stops the running reply".
What the code does today: No turn name exists. The agent queues a message that arrives during a busy turn. The pane draws the message at once and adds every part at the bottom, so the bug is real. Accepting this card means a code change.

I built the prototype and opened it in your browser: `.werk/prototypes/werk-chat-turn-id.html`. I also posted the link on #werk-chat-turn-id. I checked a screenshot, and all five steps display correctly.

The page has five steps. Each step puts the chat pane today (left) next to the chat pane with turn names (right):

1. **Message A is sent.** The first part of reply A streams. Both panes look the same.
2. **Message B is sent while reply A streams.** Both panes draw B at the bottom at once. On the right, B also shows a "waits for the reply above" mark. This mark is the open question.
3. **More parts of reply A arrive.** Today they go under B and read as the answer to B. With turn names they go above B.
4. **Reply A ends.** Today reply B runs on from reply A with nothing between them. With turn names reply B starts under B, and the waiting mark goes away.
5. **Both replies are done.** With turn names the chat reads as two question-and-answer pairs.

The page shows which part arrives in each step with an amber outline. The "reply A" and "reply B" labels are only for the prototype. The product does not draw them.

Next: do you want the waiting mark from step 2? If yes, I add it to the card before you accept it.

why: A person can send a second message while a reply still streams. The pane draws that message at once. If the pane adds each new part of the reply at the bottom, the rest of the first reply reads as the answer to the second message.

To keep a reply under its own message, every message the person sends gets a turn name when the browser sends it. A turn is one message from the person and the whole reply to it, up to the line that ends it with duration and cost (see #werk-progress).

The agent of a conversation runs one turn at a time. The server keeps the turns that are sent and not yet ended, in the order they were sent. Each part of the agent's reply belongs to the oldest of these turns. The end line closes that turn, and the next turn starts. The live channel carries the turn name with each part, and the pane adds the part to that turn.

Two edge cases:

- The agent exits before it ends its turns. Each open turn gets the exit as its end, so no turn waits forever.
- A part arrives for a turn that this page did not send, for example after a reload. The pane starts a new turn for it.

Example:

- Message A "Summarise the open cards" is sent. Its reply streams.
- Message B "Also list the ghosts" is sent while the reply to A streams.

1. The pane draws A, then the first part of reply A under it.
2. The person sends B. The pane draws B below reply A. The server holds B, because A has not ended.
3. A second part of reply A arrives. The pane adds it under A, above B.
4. The end line of A arrives. A closes, and the agent starts B.
5. The first part of reply B arrives. The pane adds it under B.

  part 2 -> A                 a2     <- step 3: lands above B

#werk-chat-turn-id is built. If you send a second message while a reply streams, the rest of the first reply now stays above it. The second message shows "waits for the reply above" until its turn starts.

To see it, run `npm run dev`. Send a long request, then send a second message before the reply ends.

**Checks:**
- **Tests:** four new agent tests cover the turns, and they pass. The full suite has 778 passing tests and 1 failure. The failing test is the overseer test "a failed read starts the flat window again". It failed once in three runs of its own file, and it does not use the chat code.
- **Lint:** clean.
- **Browser:** I drove the real pane with scripted live events. I did not use a real agent. Reply A, with a tool call, stayed above message B, and B showed the waiting mark. After A's end line, the mark went away and reply B started under B.
- **Not checked:** I did not run a real two-message turn against a live agent.

**Changes you will notice:**
- If the agent stops or exits, every open turn ends. A message that was waiting is dropped. Before, a waiting message stayed in a queue and was never sent.
- Messages in an old transcript have no turn name. They display as before.

My first version broke `web/app.js` in the browser. I added a second `isRunning`, and the file already had one. Another session reported it, and I renamed mine to `turnRunning`. The page loads now.
